The last two weeks have seen something of a media frenzy concerning the car bombing death of Darya Dugina , which most people assume was really targeted at her father, Russian ultranationalist ideologue Alexander Dugin. This sketch is skewed in Dugin's favour because it forgets to add "pro-genocide," which father and daughter certainly were (and in Dugin's case, still is).

hlead: Daughter of Russian philosopher Alexander Dugin, Putin's "mastermind," killed in explosion Daria Dugina, daughter of Russian philosopher Alexander Dugin, died Saturday night when the car she was driving exploded near the village of Bolshie Vyazyomy, in the Moscow region, local media reported.Several reports said that the explosion could be an attack, possibly directed against the intellectual with ties to the Kremlin, considered the "brain" of Russian President Vladimir Putin.Social networks were filled with images of Dugin at the scene, holding his hands to his head in front of the burning car.Witnesses said that at around 21.45 local time the vehicle suffered a loud explosion while on the road and filled the whole area with debris. The car then crashed into a fence before being completely engulfed in flames. "A Toyota Land Cruiser Prado blew up in the village of Bolshie Vyazyomy, on the outskirts of Moscow.

Local newspapers pointed out that the Emergency services were unable to identify the body of the person who was driving, as it was completely burnt.Daria, 30 years old, who was dedicated to journalism, philosophy and political science, had been included on June 4, 2022 in the list of those sanctioned by the United Kingdom against Russian personalities in retaliation for the invasion of Ukraine for "providing support or promoting policies" to destabilize the country presided by Volodimir Zelenski.The authorities have not commented on the matter for the moment, but the separatist head of the Donetsk People's Republic in eastern Ukraine, Denis Pushilin, wrote on his Telegram account that behind the attack are "terrorists of the Ukrainian regime" who were trying to kill Dugin.Dugin, also known as "Putin's Rasputin" by the international press, is the de facto author of Putin's Ukrainian strategy. Although he holds no official government position - he is more of a part-time academic and former editor-in-chief of Tsargrad TV, a network known for its fervent support of both Putin and the Russian Orthodox Church - he has been perpetually cagey about the details of his relationship with the Russian leader.

With the new escalation of Vladimir Putin, who is preparing to illegally annex four regions of the neighboring country, which remains partially or fully occupied, Brussels is proposing a new wave of sanctions to which it wants to add thirty names that will be banned from entering EU territory and will see their assets frozen, and seven companies. In the list proposed to the Member States, to which EL PAÍS has had access, there are names such as the Russian ultranationalist philosopher Alexander Dugin, one of the main current ideologues of Russian imperialism, the puppet authorities that Moscow has placed in the Ukrainian regions that it is preparing to annex illegally, as well as a good number of deputy defense ministers.

Daria Dugina, 30, was known for her activity as a political commentator and was sanctioned by the UK for "providing support or promoting policies to destabilize Ukraine ." "The crime was planned and committed by the Ukrainian special services," the Russian espionage has assured through a statement in which it has even given names and surnames to the alleged perpetrator - a Ukrainian citizen, according to the FSB - of an attack that happened in a place where the cameras installed everywhere throughout Russia had stopped working days before. hlead: Russia blames Ukrainian secret services for murder of Kremlin ideologue Dugin's daughter The Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) claims to have solved in less than 48 hours the murder of Daria Dugina, the daughter of the ultra-nationalist philosopher Alexander Dugin, who died this Saturday when a bomb attached to the underbody of the car she was driving exploded near Bolshie Viaziomy, about 40 kilometers from Moscow. "The crime was planned and committed by the Ukrainian special services," the Russian espionage has assured through a statement in which it has even given names and surnames to the alleged perpetrator - a Ukrainian citizen, according to the FSB - of an attack that happened in a place where the cameras installed everywhere throughout Russia had stopped working days before. The accusation threatens to further raise tensions between Moscow and Kiev, two days before August 24, when it will be six months since Russia 's invasion of Ukraine and at a time when Ukrainian President Volodymir Zelensky warns that Russia is preparing an offensive on that date.

hlead: Kiev considers Russian accusation that Ukrainian serviceman murdered Dugin's daughter a fabrication The Russian secret services have not hesitated to point the finger at the Ukrainian authorities for being behind the murder in Moscow of the ultranationalist political scientist Daria Dugina. The person accused by the Kremlin of having committed the bomb attack on the car in which the victim was traveling is a 43-year-old Ukrainian woman. Several photographs of this person, Natalia Vovk, and also an alleged document identifying her as a member of the Ukrainian National Guard, the military division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and the Azov regiment, were circulated in Russian media and social accounts on Monday. The version of events drawn up by the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) sows multiple suspicions accompanied by an avalanche of propaganda. For the Ukrainian Interior Ministry, the Kremlin is trying to inflame the Russian mood with false information about a Ukraine in the hands of extremists and terrorists.

Nemesis pointed to Vovk as a member of the Azov Regiment, a far-right paramilitary group currently under the orders of the National Guard. Both representatives of Azov and the National Guard have denied that this person was a member of the regiment. The Azov regiment, foundationally ultranationalist, is one of the main resources of Russian propaganda to draw Ukraine as a country dominated by fascist hordes. A spokesman for the National Guard told EL PAÍS that they will check if the identity document is authentic. The Prosecutor General's Office assured Pravda newspaper that it could be that this document was stolen by the invaders in Mariupol, a city occupied by Russia and from where the military woman Vovk allegedly came from.

hlead: Kiev considers Russian accusation that Ukrainian serviceman murdered Dugin's daughter a fabrication The Russian secret services have not hesitated to point the finger at the Ukrainian authorities for being behind the murder in Moscow of the ultranationalist political scientist Daria Dugina. The person accused by the Kremlin of having committed the bomb attack on the car in which the victim was traveling is a 43-year-old Ukrainian woman. Several photographs of this person, Natalia Vovk, and also an alleged document identifying her as a member of the Ukrainian National Guard, the military division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and the Azov regiment, were circulated in Russian media and social accounts on Monday. The version of events drawn up by the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) sows multiple suspicions accompanied by an avalanche of propaganda. For the Ukrainian Interior Ministry, the Kremlin is trying to inflame the Russian mood with false information about a Ukraine in the hands of extremists and terrorists.

headline: Russia accused Ukraine for journalist Dugina's crime
hlead: Russia accused Ukraine for journalist Dugina's crime Russia officially blamed Ukraine for the attack that killed journalist Daria Dugina. According to the Russian intelligence service FSB, "the crime was planned and committed by the Ukrainian special services" . The FSB , the heir to the dreaded Soviet KGB, says that the alleged perpetrator of Daria Dugina's murder is a woman who fled to Estonia after blowing up the car . She is reportedly Ukrainian citizen Natalia Vovk (born in 1979) who arrived in Russia on July 23 with her 12-year-old daughter Sofia Shaban . The FSB points her out as a suspect in the murder. The investigation claims that Dugina was followed in a Mini Cooper car, which had its license plates changed three times with license plates from Kazakhstan, Ukraine and the self-proclaimed Republic of Donetsk. From that car the explosive placed in Dugina's vehicle was remotely detonated .

hlead: Russia accused Ukraine for journalist Dugina's crime Russia officially blamed Ukraine for the attack that killed journalist Daria Dugina. According to the Russian intelligence service FSB, "the crime was planned and committed by the Ukrainian special services" . The FSB , the heir to the dreaded Soviet KGB, says that the alleged perpetrator of Daria Dugina's murder is a woman who fled to Estonia after blowing up the car . She is reportedly Ukrainian citizen Natalia Vovk (born in 1979) who arrived in Russia on July 23 with her 12-year-old daughter Sofia Shaban . The FSB points her out as a suspect in the murder. The investigation claims that Dugina was followed in a Mini Cooper car, which had its license plates changed three times with license plates from Kazakhstan, Ukraine and the self-proclaimed Republic of Donetsk. From that car the explosive placed in Dugina's vehicle was remotely detonated .

sentence: But the bloodshed gave rise to suspicions that the intended target was her father, Alexander Dugin, a nationalist philosopher and writer. Dugin is a prominent proponent of the "Russian world" concept, a spiritual and political ideology that emphasizes traditional values, the restoration of Russia's power and the unity of all ethnic Russians throughout the world. He is also a vehement supporter of Russian President Vladimir Putin's move sending troops into Ukraine. The explosion took place as his daughter was returning from a cultural festival she had attended with him. Russian media reports cited witnesses as saying the SUV belonged to Dugin and that he had decided at the last minute to travel in another vehicle. Denis Pushilin, president of the separatist Donetsk People's Republic, the pro-Moscow region that is a focus of Russia's fighting in Ukraine, blamed the blast on "terrorists of the Ukrainian regime, trying to kill Alexander Dugin." Mykhailo Podolyak, an adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, denied Ukrainian involvement, saying, "We are not a criminal state, unlike Russia, and definitely not a terrorist state." While Dugin's exact ties to Putin are unclear, the Kremlin frequently echoes rhetoric from his writings and appearances on Russian state TV. He helped popularize the "Novorossiya," or "New Russia," concept that Russia used to justify the 2014 annexation of Ukraine's Crimean Peninsula and its support of separatist rebels in eastern Ukraine. He promotes Russia as a country of piety, traditional values and authoritarian leadership, and disdains Western liberal values. His daughter expressed similar views and had appeared as a commentator on the nationalist TV channel Tsargrad, where Dugin had served as chief editor. Dugina herself was sanctioned by the United States in March for her work as chief editor of United World International, a website that the U.S. described as a disinformation source. The sanctions announcement cited a United World article this year that contended Ukraine would "perish" if it were admitted to NATO. In an appearance on Russian television just Thursday, Dugina said, "People in the West are living in a dream, in a dream given to them by global hegemony." She called America "a zombie society" in which people opposed Russia but could not find it on a map. An unknown Russian group, the National Republican Army, claimed responsibility Sunday for the bombing, according to a former Russian lawmaker, Ilya Ponomarev. The AP could not verify the existence of the group. Ponomarev, who left Russia after voting against its annexation of Crimea in 2014, made the statement to Ukrainian TV.

hlead: Blast kills Russian theorist's daughter FILE - In this photo taken on Thursday, Aug. 11, 2016, Alexander Dugin, the neo-Eurasianist ideologue, sits in his TV studio in central Moscow, Russia . The daughter of this Russian nationalist ideologist who is often referred to as "Putin's brain", was killed when her car exploded on the outskirts of Moscow, officials said Sunday, Aug. 21, 2022. ( AP Photo/Francesca Ebel, File) In this handout photo taken from video released by Investigative Committee of Russia on Sunday, Aug. 21, 2022, investigators work on the site of explosion of a car driven by Daria Dugina outside Moscow. Daria Dugina, the daughter of Alexander Dugin, the Russian nationalist ideologist often called "Putin's brain", was killed when her car exploded on the outskirts of Moscow, officials said Sunday. The Investigate Committee branch for the Moscow region said the Saturday night blast was caused by a bomb planted in the SUV driven by Daria Dugina.(Investigative Committee of Russia via AP ) In this handout photo taken from video released by Investigative Committee of Russia on Sunday, Aug. 21, 2022, investigators work on the site of explosion of a car driven by Daria Dugina outside Moscow. Daria Dugina, the daughter of Alexander Dugin, the Russian nationalist ideologist often called "Putin's brain", was killed when her car exploded on the outskirts of Moscow, officials said Sunday. The Investigate Committee branch for the Moscow region said the Saturday night blast was caused by a bomb planted in the SUV driven by Daria Dugina. (Investigative Committee of Russia via AP ) TV commentator's father known as 'Putin's brain' MOSCOW - The daughter of an influential Russian political theorist often referred to as "Putin's brain" was killed in a car bombing on the outskirts of Moscow, authorities said Sunday.

hlead: Murder of Putin ally's daughter sparks wave of outrage in Russia The bomb attack in which Daria Dugina, daughter of the Russian nationalist philosopher Alexander Dugin, was killed, generated a wave of indignation in the local political class, which directly accuses Ukraine and demands that the crime should not go unpunished. The Ukrainian authorities, for their part, deny any involvement in the attack. Dugin is credited with being the spiritual guide of the Russian invasion of Ukraine and is often described as Putin's mastermind. In 2015 he was sanctioned by the United States for his alleged involvement in the Russian annexation of Crimea. His daughter Dugina was born in 1992 and studied philosophy at Moscow State University. People close to the family maintain that the target of Saturday's bombing was actually Dugin, as Dugina was driving her father's car at the time of the explosion.

hlead: Russia shocked by murder of Putin's ideologue's daughter Russia blamed Ukraine for the murder of the daughter of a nationalist theorist whose ideas have given the Kremlin support for invading Ukraine . The young journalist Daria Dugina was killed when a bomb exploded under the car she was driving near Moscow. Ukraine said it "is not a terrorist state, like Russia, and had nothing to do" with the explosion that Saturday night killed Dugina, 29, the daughter of Alexander Dugin, a writer who is one of Vladimir Putin's ideological mentors .  He was saved by chance: he had planned to return from an event in her honor on the outskirts of Moscow in the car his daughter was using, which he owned. In the Russian language, the feminine ending of the surname adds a final "a": hence Daria is called Dugina instead of Dugin, like her father.
